identical_discrete_predictions_reason.temporal_lstm: Mode collapse to Class 0 (100% of test predictions are 0) due to severe class imbalance (85.3% normal in train) and insufficient loss weights [1.0, 1.5, 2.0] vs balanced [1.0, 11.5, 11.8]. Continuous probabilities differ (max diff: 0.1515, mean diff: 0.0343), but argmax maps 100% to 0.
identical_discrete_predictions_reason.compact_transformer: Conservative collapse where only 3 specific windows (out of 1,025) of entity 6238841354_6 exceed Class 0. Both 7B and 7D predicted Class 2 on exactly those 3 windows and Class 0 on the remaining 1,022 windows. Continuous probabilities differ (max diff: 0.2353, mean diff: 0.0328, PR-AUC warning 0.2290 vs 0.2219, critical 0.2635 vs 0.2623).

verified_facts.dataset_row_ordering_difference: Phase 7B and Phase 7D test prediction CSVs contain the exact same 1,025 (entity_id, timestamp) pairs, but in a different sort order. When aligned by (entity_id, timestamp), Random Forest agrees on 94.05% of windows (61 diffs) and Hybrid agrees on 91.90% (83 diffs).

confirmed_defects_and_mismatches.description: Random Forest and Representation Hybrid utilized class_weight='balanced' (assigning ~11.5x and ~11.8x penalty to Warning and Critical classes), whereas Temporal LSTM and Compact Temporal Transformer were restricted to hardcoded weights [1.0, 1.5, 2.0] (assigning only 1.5x and 2.0x penalty). This left the neural loss function 76.9% dominated by normal samples, inducing majority-class mode collapse.

configs/default_config.yaml specified a combined failure risk decision rule: P(WARNING) + P(CRITICAL) >= theta (theta=0.50). In contrast, Protocol v2.0 enforced standard 3-class argmax. Under argmax, probability mass split between Warning and Critical causes the model to predict Normal even when total failure probability exceeds 50% (median failure probability on true failures in Transformer was 57.17%, yet argmax selected Normal).

default_config.yaml specifies L=15 (75 min history), but Phase 6.1 feasibility analysis proved real-world Borg failure tasks have short lifespans (<75 min), necessitating L=5 (25 min history). At L=5, temporal recurrent and self-attention models possess minimal sequence context over static tabular features.

unresolved_hypotheses.title: Loss Weighting Rectification
unresolved_hypotheses.statement: Training Temporal LSTM and Compact Transformer with true balanced inverse-frequency weights [1.0, 11.46, 11.80] or Focal Loss will eliminate majority-class mode collapse and improve Validation Macro-F1.

unresolved_hypotheses.title: Combined Risk Thresholding
unresolved_hypotheses.statement: Switching from 3-class argmax to validation-calibrated combined failure thresholding (P(Warning) + P(Critical) >= theta_val) will enable Transformer and Hybrid to detect failure episodes without triggering prohibitive false alarms.

unresolved_hypotheses.title: Parent-Job Workload Domain Shift
unresolved_hypotheses.statement: The primary ceiling on False Alarm Rates across all architectures is cross-job workload domain shift between the 37 training parent jobs and the 12 validation / 11 test parent jobs.
